text:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; mines are located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Aha! So this story caught your interest too? It used to be our Imperial mine. Hundreds of goblins, under the watchful guidance and loud cursing of the foremen, dug up valuable strategic resources there! Well, there were some other natives too, who lived in the caves — kobolds and mountainfolk — but by special order of the Committee number... oh, I don't remember, 123\16-BIS or something, all the natives were made honorary citizens of the Empire and obliged to labor for the good of the country. And those rascals didn't want to work! No notion of discipline whatsoever. No faith in the bright future! Lazybones! They conspired with one terribly clever goblin — Ghim the Greedy, they call him — won the trolls over to their side, and drove out all the foremen, engineers and bookkeepers! Now they have something there that's either a monarchy or a commune, and Ghim is their boss. He caved in all the tunnels, raked up a pile of gold for himself, and sits there chuckling — he has beaten the Empire, you see, the scoundrel. But it's not all cakes and ale for the cat! There are still goblins on the island loyal to the Empire, a squad of bang-bang demolishers. They'll blast a tunnel through any rock! With their help you'll easily reach the lair of that separatist and plunderer of the people's economy, Ghim the Greedy. Whatever treasure you find is yours. And deliver Ghim a stern reprimand, on behalf of the whole working class, with an entry in his skull. The Empire will not forget you!

Bosses: Wick, Stakh Quickpick, Stonegnawer, Ghim the Greedy.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by … .

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Old Loam? And why are you interested? Look me in the eye! Don't dodge!

Hm... I suppose one can discuss state secrets with you. Of course I know about that island. There's nothing particularly remarkable about it — a village of poor peasants, a pine forest, a cold climate. That's probably exactly why the Committee chose it as a testing ground for its experiments. Observing Kanians in their everyday environment! Reconnaissance operations! Espionage! Ah, it reminds me of my old days... All I've heard from the sailors is that strange things began happening to the animals in the forest near Old Loam, and some of the villagers vanished without a trace. My advice is to give the island a wide berth and keep out of the Committee's affairs. Otherwise, heaven forbid, they'll have to kill you. That would be awkward. You don't have any doubt that their actions are aimed solely at the good of the Empire, do you?

Bosses: Hut, Snezhana Zaykina, Bewitched Peasant, Veres.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by pirates.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

At the dawn of astral navigation, when there were no visors yet and the first ships groped their way through the astral almost by touch, lighthouses were built on the islands that were discovered. A lighthouse's light could be seen from very far away, and it signaled: "Sail here, it's safe." Many sailors lost in the astral thanked fate more than once for a lighthouse glimpsed in the distance. Later, as astral navigation developed, lighthouses became less important. With a modern visor, astrolabe and navigator, getting lost in the astral is practically impossible. So nowadays lighthouses are for the most part a tribute to tradition and a place where you can rest in peace, spend the night and hear the latest news. But recently I received unpleasant news: a gang of astral pirates has seized one of the old lighthouses and is using it as a trap. As soon as a ship heading for the lighthouse's light moors at the pier, it is boarded at once, plundered and smashed to splinters, and the whole crew is sent to walk the plank into the astral! Beasts! Barbarians! So many innocent people have suffered because of them. They must be stopped at any cost! And the treasures, if you find them, keep for yourself — the dead have no use for them anymore...

Bosses: Zavid Ushkuynikov, Yasskul "Jolly" Roger, Sturdy Door, Feint the Greedy.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former Kanian settlement, now inhabited by the undead.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The island of Silent Hills always served me as proof that in the future we and the Kanians will be able to live in peace. I didn't visit it often, but when I did, I talked without fear to simple Kanians tending their modest farms, and stocked up on their freshly baked, extraordinarily tasty bread. They didn't care a whit about the feud between Tensess and Nezeb, about the war between the League and the Empire... Now ghosts are the masters there. They go about their business as before: they fish, hunt, grind flour. And they were not at all glad to see either me or my crew. We barely got away. I am at a loss! What evil has appeared in Silent Hills? Who cursed the poor souls? If you have the courage to take up the challenge of this mystery, follow my advice. Look for the cause of Silent Hills' misfortunes in the dark forest! The peasants always gave that place a wide berth. Perhaps one of them broke the age-old order and woke the evil slumbering there. Obstacles will surely stand in your way, and you'll have to overcome them to reach the source of the evil. Remember that you won't manage to cleanse the island without fighting its ghostly inhabitants. That is the pain you'll have to go through. Know that you bring them not death, but release from the Darkness.

Bosses: Tsar Pike, Elder Miller, the Bane of Silent Hills.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by forest fauna and spirits.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Isle of Far-Far-Away? Hm... As an acquaintance of mine put it: "Calm, smooth, and the grace of Tensess." And where does such a strange name come from? Well, it's a funny story. Long ago, before the Cataclysm, one remote Kanian province had a name so jaw-breaking that it wasn't preserved even in official charters. And the inhabitants themselves jokingly called their land the Kingdom of Far-Far-Away. It was a real backwater... Forest, forest and nothing but forest! Thousands of hectares of solid green. And it was ruled by a guardian — the living soul of the forest. They say whoever entered that forest with ill thoughts never came out again. Well, after the Cataclysm only a pitiful scrap of that forest remained. But it held out and did not melt away in the astral. And the guardian, they say, survived too. Knowledgeable people told me that her magic still protects the island. Every traveler can count on shelter and rest under the canopy of the age-old trees. But Light forbid you anger the mistress of the forest! If you try to turn the local animals into shashlik, you won't have time to blink before you're turned into cutlets yourself.

Bosses: Forest Spirit, Veleslav Dubov, Blackmarin, Forest Guardian.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians and elves.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

An interesting little place. I haven't been there for a long while... And no wish to go, to be honest. Just a few years ago Triplefield was a lively trading town. What didn't they sell at the local market — elven gems, peasant bast shoes, Kanian armor... And then some disaster befell them: the dead rose and devoured the whole town, and few survived. The survivors brought down the only bridge leading to the town and settled in a small village some way off from the cursed ruins. Fortunately, the elves, whose enclave was nearby, were not affected by the curse that fell upon the town, and helped the surviving people set up at least some kind of peaceful life. But Triplefield will never see its former glory — now it's just a backwater hole. Still, I've heard that the League Church recently sent a squad of inquisitors there, and now I'm wondering — what could churchmen have lost in that Light-forsaken place?

Bosses: Alister de Doucer, Mstislav Ferocious, Milava Troepolskaya, Alex Gordev.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Desert, closest to Kirah.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

You probably know what happened on Irdrich. Tep, an ancient necromancer of the Zem people, fancied himself a god and prepared a whole army of mechanoids to enslave all of Sarnaut. In the face of such danger our troops joined forces with the Leaguers and crushed the viper after all. But though Tep is dead, his cause lives on. Every now and then heroes stumble upon lairs of cultists who don't know about the death of their god or refuse to believe in it. And sometimes it's the other way round: some of Tep's slaves turned away from their master. One soldier told me that while the cultists and mechanoids were hacking away at the united army, a rusty barge quietly pulled away from the shore and sailed off in an unknown direction. Maybe it's just a tall tale: I sell it for what I bought it. But if you come across an island of rusty renegades somewhere in the depths of the astral, don't be surprised.

Bosses: Fill-o-Matic, Nomarkh Megavolt, Negus Augment, Integral.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Wasteland, closest to the Cradle.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Overlord's servants.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know about this island only from scraps of information that fell into the hands of Imperial intelligence. In short, it went like this. In one of the sectors an Imperial reconnaissance ship discovered an island not marked on the maps. The captain made several ferrotypes of the island and sent them as an urgent message to the capital. The message said that the captain had decided to carry out reconnaissance. They have not made contact since. You see, this island, which was given the name the Jail, is the prison of the Overlord himself! The ferrotypes show exhausted prisoners locked inside energy domes, and all the passages are blocked by force fields. The territory is patrolled by the Overlord's close servants and battle machines. What's more, there are creatures there that the Committee's experts have identified as high-ranking Wormfaces. According to their theory, it is they who are running what goes on in the Jail at the moment. Which, you'll agree, is somewhat strange — after all, the Wormfaces betrayed the Overlord. From this I can draw one certain conclusion and two guesses. The conclusion: the island is the Overlord's prison, where his servants keep undesirable adventurers. The guesses are these. First, the Wormfaces have somehow managed to subjugate the Overlord's servants. Second, they are hiding from everyone, and we will most likely never see the crew that landed on the shore again. I wouldn't advise you to go there without the support of at least one battleship, or better two. Some mysteries are better never solved...

Bosses: Bloody Executioner, Farakh, the Overlord's Punishment, Provost.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, where Imperial outlaws have settled.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, I know about that island. How could I not? A decent little place... If you're ready to put up with quacking that doesn't stop for a minute! There's a Kanian village there, and every house has ducks beyond counting. They salt duck, bake it, dry it and sell it. Even the pillow in my cabin is stuffed with local down. It's like lying down to sleep on a cloud... But a misfortune has befallen them. Have you heard about the recent escape from the maximum security zone? No? Strange... It was in all the papers. A whole gang of convicts, mostly orcs and goblins, slaughtered the guards, seized a ship and made off in an unknown direction. They called themselves the "Tribe of the Daring" and set about robbing, wrecking and burning everything in their path. Lawless thugs, what else can I say. They boarded several of our ships, robbed them down to the last frame, and threw the crews overboard. They wiped out an outpost in the far astral root and branch — the Committee's investigators came back from there green as frogs and swearing like cobblers. And the last thing I heard about that gang is that they stumbled upon Duck River Run. Well, the locals are out of luck. I'm afraid even to imagine what lawlessness is going on there now!

Bosses: Torch the Daring, Haze the Daring, Rod the Daring, Chopper the Daring.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Howlem.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, an ancient abode of the Pridens.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Ravine of Shadows? I've heard of it, I've heard. I haven't been there myself, I won't lie. But a Priden traveler told me that long, long ago — so long that even their Voices barely remember when it was — a huge piece broke off from Howlem, and on it stood some temple. The Pridens believe they angered the First Ones, and the First Ones punished them. I don't know about the curse of the First Ones, but I've heard from astral pirates about a huge mountain in the astral with old ruins rising on its summit. Gentlemen of fortune tried to pick up something valuable there, and barely got away. In a whisper they told how their own shadows came to life and began killing right and left. And when the whole pirate rabble scattered in all directions, ghosts — whether of men or beasts, who knows — stood in their path with weapons in their hands, and not a single one reached the ruins alive. Those who managed to rush back to the ship raced away from that island under full sail. So I reckon that if it was a curse, it still haunts anyone who dares to enter this Ravine...

Bosses: Forgotten, Maas-Risa the Bedazzling, Saad-Brok the Stormbringer, Shoom-Kagat the Black-Handed.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a laboratory is located here.

Story:
Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

This island belongs to Nomarkh Iblis, an oligarch and inventor. He's a rich man, well known, but not very respected. He's far too fond of inventing schemes to cheat his partners instead of weapons. Only last time he picked the wrong target: he had the gall to swindle Yasker himself. Yasker wouldn't swallow the insult, and as soon as his scouts found the island, he sent a whole battalion there. How it all ended, I don't know. In my opinion, it didn't: the Imperial soldiers are strong, but you can't take a factory stuffed to the roof with weapons in one rush either. We Leaguers have nothing to do there — except maybe watch the show from afar. Want to make a bet? I'll put ten gold on the Imperials not pulling it off!

Story allod:

Catherina sent the Heroes to search for Yelisseus Korolev. And only his old nanny knew where he was. It turned out that Yelisseus had disappeared on the Death Plant island: he had gone there to learn from Nomarkh Iblis, the Oligarch, where to find his beloved Annette. Setting off after Yelisseus, the heroes met on the island Leila Snoop, a Committee operative who had picked up the trail of a sinister conspiracy.

This very Nomarkh Iblis, one of the seven Oligarchs who rule the Free Traders, grew rich on the arms trade. All those turrets, mechanisms and other weapons that have flooded Sarnaut in recent years are his handiwork. But the trouble lay elsewhere. Not long ago Iblis put a new weapon on sale — the Spinners. And on every one of the Spinners he installed a remote-control device. At one fine moment the Spinners were to rise against their owners, and Iblis would become the ruler of all Sarnaut. Leila offered to thwart his plans. Long and bloody was the path through the laboratories and workshops of the Death Plant; the Xadaganian scout herself fell victim (or so it seemed at the time); and Yelisseus was found, whom Iblis had wanted to turn into a mechanical bogatyr. For it turned out that all of Catherina's guard, the bogatyrs, had been remade from heroes, and inside the mechanical bodies were the Sparks of the living. The heroes fought their way out of the dungeons with Yelisseus, finished off Iblis himself, and on his body found documents proving that he had been cooperating with Catherina. She did not deny it, and admitted that she had needed Iblis for his technologies. "Engineers with powerful manatrons, a flying tower, the best shipyard in the world and my mechanical guard — none of this came out of thin air."

Bosses: Yasskul Samekh, Modified Orc, Ghost of Yaver Khess, Polytoc Hexnut.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian settlement seized by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

You know about that one too? Hm... Strictly speaking, it isn't an island at all. It's a giant turtle that swims eternally through the astral. It's so enormous that a whole village lives on its back! Or rather, lived... Here's the thing... Two noblemen, the Zalesky brothers, mighty sorcerers, decided that the present authorities didn't suit them. They resolved to raise a revolt — for selfish reasons, of course. But Aidenus quickly learned of the treachery. The brothers gathered their retinue, loaded onto a ship and dashed off wherever their eyes led them. And their eyes spotted Turtle Island. They moored at the shore; the peasants saw the lordly ship and greeted the renegades with bread and salt, and in return the renegades put them to a cruel death! Only a few hunters managed to flee and hide in the astral. They were picked up by a Kanian ship belonging to my friend, Afanasy Nikitov. And he told me this story. As I understand it, the brothers are now trying to bend the flying turtle to their will. Can you imagine what will happen if they succeed? If someone sent those brothers to their graves, I'd have nothing but thanks for that hero!

Bosses: Tikhon Yezhov, Hardshell, Gostemil Zalesky, Velerad Zalesky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Wasteland, closest to Yazes Shard.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Demons.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Black Rock... You'll recognize it the moment you approach the island! A lifeless shard of bare stone, gnawed by demonic fangs. It's simply swarming with demons! As far as I know, the Black Rock is all that remains of the allod of the House de Blizare after the Night of Astral Portals. The House de Blizare suffered enormous losses that night. Almost all their mages died in battle; the Great Mage lost his nerve and prepared to open a portal to Kania, which finally broke the fighting spirit of the defenders. The elves fled, leaving their allod to be torn apart by the demons. However, for some reason I can't understand, the allod turned out to be extraordinarily resistant to the effects of the astral. They say the blood of the elven martyrs who defended their home to the last is the cause... But I don't believe it! Elves are deceitful and selfish creatures who know nothing of heroic self-sacrifice. Although by their standards such a death would surely count as beautiful. In short, the Black Rock is now a piece of land crawling with demons. There are as many of them as fleas on a goblin! So I strongly advise you not even to go near this island. An armada of demons is not the enemy you want to run into in the astral!

Bosses: Gryzl, Bonegrinder, Hornbearer, Sparky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by traders and Kanians.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, Plague City is a bad business. Of course, it wasn't always called that — once it was a perfectly ordinary, flourishing city, moderately rich, decently arranged; its rulers even had heads on their shoulders. Not every backwater can manage that, you know — develop some kind of trade, give children an education and keep a firm faith in the Light. In short, it was an outstanding city. And every outstanding thing will have its envious ones. Sometimes, alas, very powerful ones. For some reason a certain warlock came to hate this city — and he had power enough to release the Pestilence, a merciless magical disease that turned the city into an abode of nightmares within a matter of hours. Some tried to fight — to burn the contagion with fire. Others "adapted" and began quickly hauling off everything of value. And the third... They were less lucky — the disease took them, turning them into mindless undead. In the end the cursed city broke away from the allod and was lost in the astral. You can see it here and there — the curse of the Pestilence forces it to relive that terrible day over and over. With all my heart I wish you never to become its witness.

Bosses: Hur the Boiling, Long Arm, Yaver Brand, Devastator.

Type: Medium allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a Kanian settlement.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know the place. Only I strongly advise against flying there! On that island there's a whole village of religious fanatics. Unwashed peasants who, not so long ago, meekly grew turnips for the Kanian soldiery have imagined themselves heaven knows what. They've rejected faith in the Light, not to mention the veneration of Saints Nezeb and Skrakan, and worship some kind of nature spirits. And their leader is the magus Jaromir. It was he, the bearded lunatic, who incited all the peasants to revolt! He's completely addled the village men's heads with his tales about the faith of their ancestors, the greatness of ancient Kania, the glorious Traditions... No, honoring traditions is sacred. But with some sense! We're building mana stations and underground railways, the League is treading on our heels in developing industry, and they're still living in the last millennium. A wild people, in a word — not like us, the enlightened citizens of the great Empire. So if the road leads you to Clear Mountain, get ready to fight the whole village at once. And the local bogatyrs too. Alexei, Ivan and Vladislav, hulking brutes — step out of line and they'll hammer you into the ground up to your ears. But if you manage to defeat Jaromir himself, maybe the peasants will come to their senses and stop grabbing every stranger and throwing him into the astral...

Bosses: Aunt Agafya, Vladislav the Cruel, Prokopy, Jaromir.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the undead.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. I think you know no worse than I do about the ill fame of this place. The patrimony of the noblest aristocrats turned into a den of unclean spirits and the undead. Or rather, so it was until a squad of League daredevils made their way into the very depths of that burrow and put an end to the curse. But what if everything had gone wrong? The mysterious astral is an enigmatic place. Sometimes it lets you see what would have become of familiar places if history had developed differently. The Imperials have nothing to do in Castle Blight — they have troubles enough of their own. But what if Kania had fallen under the rule of the Empire? What if Elizaveta Rysina had sent an elite corps of exorcists to the castle, and the evil entrenched in the castle had taken possession of their souls? If you find yourself in the reflection of Castle Blight, beware: those you meet there are not real priests, not Imperials, and not even people. But the wounds they can inflict on you are quite real... As are the treasures you'll find in the storerooms!

Bosses: Firebliz the Righteous, Svetlana Pravdina, Crucifier, Kirill Pravdin, the Guise-Stealer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

Climate: Desert, closest to Kirah.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the undead.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. The name of Tep no longer strikes terror into peaceful folk. This ancient Hickutian sorcerer, who longed to become a god, was destroyed by the heroes of the Empire on the shards of the allod of Irdrich, with some minor help from the brave souls of the League. But what if Tep had not been resurrected? What would have become of his lair if it had never seen its master return? They say that in the depths of the astral one can find a reflection of Irdrich where there is neither a pyramid nor cultists — only the grim inventions of the ancient necromancer, which go on wrecking ships and snuffing out Sparks even without their creator. If you come across this place, be careful: though it is only what might have happened, Tep's reflected machines are no less dangerous than the real ones!

Bosses: Mikhail Blankstare, Artem Ostankin, George Podpalin, Hungry Demon, Megalit.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Igsh.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a laboratory is located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Secret laboratories... The Committee can stamp as many secrecy classifications as it likes, but murder will out: even the lowliest goblin under a fence already knows that our research program has serious problems. Something explodes in one laboratory, something leaks in another, and in a third the head of the lab turns out to be a cultist. And the harder they try to classify it all, the more rumors go around. And rumors have a power of their own. Because the astral... The astral knows how to listen. And now in its depths you can find a reflection that embodies all the scary tales about Imperial laboratories. Mad scientists, cultist spies, inhuman experiments, nightmarish machines and mutilated test subjects — everything idle chatterboxes might spin for you. So if you see a science town behind iron gates somewhere in the astral and decide to go ashore... I hope you have strong nerves!

Bosses: Armando de Doucer, Poisonous Trap, Darksoul Leader, Purger Fire Thrower, Meat Golem.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Igsh.

Affiliation: League allod; a prison is located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Don't you really know about this place? Although... you probably have no need to. Oreshek Fortress is the largest and most impregnable prison in the whole League. They hold the most dangerous cutthroats and butchers there, thieves and swindlers, traitors and rebels. No one has ever escaped from there — where would you run to from an astral island! They say the Committee tried to carry out a special operation there: to free some dangerous rebel and drop him back onto Kania — let Aidenus have a headache. The guards turned out to be no slouches, and our people barely got away... But that's in reality! And somewhere in the depths of the astral a reflection has appeared in which the prisoner got free. And, you know, those who have seen that reflection say it's a good thing the Committee didn't succeed in reality. Unpatriotic, of course, but the last thing we needed was one of the League's mightiest fortresses turned into a bandit nest!

Bosses: Trap, Asyka, Marcel de Doucer, Daring Family, Miroslav Kramolsky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Gipat.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Wormfaces.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. An ancient temple of a vanished people... To whom did they offer prayers in it? To the One Creator? To local spirits? To great heroes and rulers? What did they sacrifice — incense or someone's hearts? Today no one knows. The temple ruins on Gipat became the stage for the last act of the Play, where the heroes of Sarnaut received the Revelation. I was there too... Now that's a place I'd rather not go back to! But one traveler told me that in the depths of the mysterious astral he saw a reflection of the June Temple: ruins where imps and demon worshippers wander. True, in that temple the cultists dug up some June magitech and are now at war with it, not knowing how to bury it again. He also let slip that at the very end the temple gave him an unpleasant surprise. If you ask me — what could be more unpleasant than what we actually found in it? But you, if you find this reflection, keep your ears open!

Bosses: Fleshwither, Inevitable Death, Ravager, Vur'tazz the Ravager, Soul Sucker.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Is it for me to tell you about Tensess Temple! After all, it was you who had to fight your way through hordes of enemies to uncover the secret of the gift of Light. I'd like to know what you heroes saw there and what the Spark of Tensess told you. But a state secret is a state secret. I'd better tell you what I know about its astral reflection.

A half-ruined sanctuary in the depths of the jungle — the tomb of an ancient mage, a rival of Nezeb himself. You won't find the Spark of Tensess in the reflection, but there will be enemies in abundance. In this the reflection is very close to reality... You'll have to overcome the most dangerous enemies and a whole horde of demons at the very top of the temple. But the reward will be worthy! Who knows, perhaps the reflection will share new secrets with you?

Bosses: Fleshwither, Inevitable Death, Ravager, Vur'tazz the Ravager, Soul Sucker.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by vampires.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. You know what happened in the Darkblood Citadel. The ancestral nest of the House de Doucer, where all high society once flocked to balls and soirées, turned into a nest of ghouls. Armando de Doucer got in league with Tep and staged a vampire invasion of Kania and Avilon. Only the intervention of heroes like you thwarted his plans... But what if everything had gone differently? Do you know who the worst enemies of vampires are? Werewolves! It seems to have something to do with the blood curse that lies on both of them. If the spires of a galleon palace appear in the mysterious astral, get ready to see what would have happened if the werewolves had got to the ghouls before the heroes of the League. Only don't let your guard down: werewolves hate the likes of you only a little less than bloodsuckers. Mind you don't end up between the hammer and the anvil!

Bosses: Ushan, Rottenfang, Webweaver, Shadow, Zinovy Gorsky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

Island size:

Small allods — the smallest allods, mostly a single settlement.

Medium islands — larger islands, usually with several large settlements.

Large islands — have many settlements and various zones and regions.

Climate:

Desert — deserts, little vegetation, palm trees.

Tropical — jungle and swampy jungle.

Temperate — meadows and forests of the middle latitudes, coniferous and deciduous forest.

Taiga — mostly coniferous trees and snow cover.

Tundra — small trees or none at all, permafrost.

Wasteland — a mixture of ordinary matter with the matter of another universe; also the astral wasteland.

Affiliation:

League — population: Kanians, Gibberlings and elves.

Imperial — population: Zem, Xadaganians and orcs.

Elven — population: elves only; not part of the League.

Neutral — population from both the League and the Empire, Free Traders and pirates. Also various lesser races (Forestfolk, lizards, etc.).
